Running it
----------
simcity.nex is a program for the ZX Spectrum Next.  Copy it to the SD card
and run it from the browser (or with the nexload command); in an emulator
such as CSpect, ZEsarUX or JNext, load it as a NEX file.  It needs a Next
with at least 512 KB of RAM and the NextZXOS (for saving and loading).

The game uses the Layer 2 screen (256 x 192).  The map and the tool icons
use the Amiga SimCity's pictures and the other screens use the Atari ST
game's colours.  The ST game's sound effects play on the AY chip.  The
Z80 runs at 14 MHz, and the game still runs at 50 frames a second.  Cities
are saved to the SD card, and loaded from it, in the current folder.

The map is 120 x 100 squares, bigger than the Spectrum game's 96 x 96.
The title screen offers the Amiga game's eight scenarios: choose one with
the left and right cursor keys, read about it with up and down, and press
Enter to play.  Each scenario has a time limit and a goal, both given in
its text.  When the time is up the game tells you whether you won or
lost, and then you can carry on in the same city.

The mini map shows 96 x 96 squares of the city, and scrolls with the
cursor keys.

Keys
----
  Cursor keys     move the cursor one square (Next cursor keys are Caps
                  Shift with 5 6 7 8); with Symbol Shift too: eight
  O P Q A         left, right, up, down (with Caps Shift: eight)
  Space, Enter    build with the tool
  , .             the previous and next tool (Symbol Shift with N and M)
  0 - 9           choose a tool by its number
  H               pause or run
  + -             faster, slower (Symbol Shift with K and J)
  M               the next mini map (X goes back to the city)
  B               the budget            V   the evaluation
  S               save the city         L   load a city
  X               the game menu: new city, options, disasters, sound
  Break, Edit     (Caps Shift with Space, or with 1) leave a screen
  Delete          (Caps Shift with 0) rubs out a letter of a file name

The mouse
---------
A Kempston mouse works with this version.
The arrow on the screen is the cursor.  The keys move it too, so you can
use either, or both, whenever you like.

  Left button     (Space or Enter on the keyboard) builds with the
                  current tool, picks a tool from the icons, chooses an
                  item in a menu, and on a mini map jumps to that spot
  Right button    (Esc) opens the game menu, and leaves a screen
  Screen edge     the map scrolls when the arrow reaches the edge

In the menus and on the budget, evaluation, file and scenario screens,
moving the mouse works like pressing the cursor keys.
